spots.name: Lighthouse of Alexandria
spots.summary: The Pharos of Alexandria was a lighthouse built by the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Ancient Egypt, during the reign of Ptolemy II Philadelphus. It has been estimated to have been at least 100 metres (330 ft) in overall height.

names.ja: アレクサンドリアの大灯台

spots.name: Library of Alexandria

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Library of Alexandria in Alexandria, Egypt, was one of the largest and most significant libraries of the ancient world. The library was part of a larger research institution called the Mouseion, which was dedicated to the Muses, the nine goddesses of the arts.

names.ja: アレクサンドリア図書館

spots.name: Citadel of Qaitbay
spots.summary: The Citadel of Qaitbay is a 15th-century defensive fortress located on the Mediterranean sea coast, on Pharos Island in Alexandria, Egypt. It was built from 1477 to 1479 AD by Sultan of Egypt al-Ashraf Sayf al-Din Qaitbay.

names.ja: カーイト・ベイの要塞

spots.name: Bibliotheca Alexandrina

hours.note: Closed Fri, Sat

spots.summary: The Bibliotheca Alexandrina (BA) is a major library and cultural center on the shore of the Mediterranean Sea in Alexandria, Egypt. It is a commemoration of the Library of Alexandria, once one of the largest libraries worldwide, which was lost in antiquity.

names.ja: 新アレクサンドリア図書館

spots.name: Alexandria National Museum
spots.summary: The Alexandria National Museum (ANM) is a museum in Alexandria, Egypt. It was inaugurated the 31 December 2003 by Hosni Mubarak and it is located in a renovated Italian style palace in Tariq Al-Horreya Street (former Rue Fouad). The building used to be home to the United States consulate.

names.zh: 亚历山大港国家博物馆

spots.name: Pompey's Pillar
spots.summary: Pompey's Pillar is a Roman triumphal column in Alexandria, Egypt. Despite its modern name, it was actually set up in honour of the Roman emperor Diocletian between 298–302 AD. The giant Corinthian column originally supported a colossal porphyry statue of the emperor in armour.

spots.name: Saint Mark's Coptic Orthodox Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint Mark's Coptic Orthodox Cathedral is a Coptic church in Alexandria, Egypt. It is the historical seat of the Pope of Alexandria, the head of the Coptic Orthodox Church.

names.es: Catedral Ortodoxa Copta de San Marcos

spots.name: Serapeum of Alexandria

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Serapeum of Alexandria was an ancient Greek temple built by Ptolemy III Euergetes and dedicated to the Greco-Egyptian syncretic god Serapis, who was believed to be the protector of Alexandria, Egypt. It was built during the 3rd century BCE, primarily between 246 and 222 BCE.

names.ja: アレクサンドリアのセラペウム

spots.name: St. Catherine's Cathedral, Alexandria

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Catherine's Cathedral is a Catholic cathedral in Alexandria, Egypt. It is the seat of the Apostolic Vicariate of Alexandria of Egypt. It also serves as the church of the Franciscan monastery in Alexandria.

photo.author: Alexandria,_Kirche_St._Katharina.jpg: Roland Unger derivative work: Rabanus Flav

spots.name: Abu al-Abbas al-Mursi Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Abu al-Abbas al-Mursi Mosque is a mosque, mausoleum, and Sufi shrine, located in the Anfoushi neighbourhood of Alexandria, on the north coast of Egypt.

names.zh: 阿布·阿巴斯·穆尔西清真寺

spots.name: Graeco-Roman Museum
spots.summary: The Graeco-Roman Museum is an archaeological museum located in Alexandria, Egypt. Its collection of over 40,000 objects includes sculptures, mosaics, woodwork, and coins.

names.ja: グレコローマン博物館

spots.name: Eliyahu Hanavi Synagogue

hours.note: Closed Fri, Sat

spots.summary: The Eliyahu Hanavi Synagogue is a synagogue, located at 69 Nabi Daniel Street, Alexandria, Egypt.

spots.name: Caesareum of Alexandria

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Caesareum of Alexandria is an ancient temple in Alexandria, Egypt. It was conceived by Cleopatra VII of the Ptolemaic kingdom, the last pharaoh of ancient Egypt, to honour her first known lover Julius Caesar or Mark Antony.

names.ja: アレクサンドリアのカエサリウム

spots.name: Alexandria Museum of Fine Arts

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Alexandria Museum of Fine Arts is a museum for Egyptian and Middle-Eastern fine art in Alexandria, Egypt. Located in the Moharam Bek neighborhood, it houses a collection of works by Egyptian artist and a selection of works from Baroque, Romanticism, Rococo and Orientalism.

spots.name: Pharos

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Pharos of Alexandria was a lighthouse built by the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Ancient Egypt, during the reign of Ptolemy II Philadelphus. It has been estimated to have been at least 100 metres (330 ft) in overall height.

spots.name: Kom El Deka

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Kom El Deka, also known as Kom el-Dikka, is a neighborhood and archaeological site in Alexandria, Egypt. Early Kom El-Dikka was a well-off residential area, and later it was a major civic center in Alexandria, with a bath complex (thermae), auditoria, and a theatre.

spots.name: Cathedral of Evangelismos

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Holy Cathedral Church of the Annunciation of the Theotokos also known as The Cathedral of the Annunciation or The Cathedral of Evangelismos is a trilateral basilica which was founded in the middle of the 19th century in Alexandria, Egypt. Its ecclesiastical see is the Patriarchate of Alexandria and All Africa.

spots.name: Sadat Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Sadat Museum is a cultural museum in Alexandria, Egypt, dedicated to the legacy of Egyptian president Anwar Al Sadat. It was inaugurated on February 17, 2009, by Suzanne Mubarak and Jehan Al Sadat and is located next to the planetarium of the Bibliotheca Alexandrina, encompassing 200 square meters.

spots.name: Alexandria Naval Unknown Soldier Memorial
spots.summary: Alexandria Naval Unknown Soldier Memorial at the Manshaya district is dedicated to the unknown soldiers who lost their lives in the sea battles, it is present on the Corniche of Alexandria.

names.ja: アレクサンドリア海軍無名戦士の記念碑

spots.name: Planetarium Science Center

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Planetarium Science Centre (PSC) is a department in the Bibliotheca Alexandrina located in Alexandria, Egypt. It promotes science centers as an educational tool.

names.ja: プラネタリウム科学センター

spots.name: Al-Busiri Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Al-Busiri Mosque, also known as Imam Al Busiri Mosque, is a mosque located in the Anfoushi neighbourhood of Alexandria, on the north coast of Egypt. The mosque is named in honour of Al-Busiri, a Sanhaji Sufi Imam who lived in Alexandria during the 13th century, and it is where his tomb is located.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Sidi Yaqut Al-Arsh Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Sidi Yaqut Al-Arsh Mosque is a mosque, located in the Anfoushi neighbourhood of Alexandria, on the north coast of Egypt. It is named after Yaqut Al Arsh, an imam who lived in Alexandria during the 13th century.

spots.name: Cavafy Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Cavafy Museum is an apartment museum in the center of Alexandria, Egypt, which formerly was the residence of the Greek poet Constantine P. Cavafy, where he lived most of his life.

spots.name: Sculpture of the sails in Alexandria

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Mausoleum of Abdullah ibn Ali Zayn al-Abidin
spots.summary: Mausoleum of Abdullah ibn Ali Zayn al-Abidin is a mausoleum dedicated to Abdullah ibn Ali Zayn al-Abidin, grandson of Husayn ibn Ali. It is located at the side of Fouad Street in the city of Alexandria, Egypt. It is located opposite of the Mausoleum of Yacoub ibn Abdul Rahman ibn Mohammed.

spots.name: Tahrir Square
spots.summary: Tahrir Square Alexandria is a public town square in Alexandria, northern Egypt.

spots.name: Mausoleum of Yacoub bin Abd al-Rahman
spots.summary: Mausoleum of Yacoub bin Abd al-Rahman is a mausoleum dedicated to Yacoub bin Abd al-Rahman, tabi'e, qāriʾ and hadith narrator. It is located at the side of Fouad Street in the city of Alexandria, Egypt. It is opposite the Mausoleum of Abdullah ibn Ali Zayn al-Abidin.

spots.name: Alexandria Stadium
spots.summary: Alexandria Stadium is a multi-purpose stadium in the Moharram Bey district of Alexandria, Egypt. It was opened in 1929 by King Fouad I. It is the oldest stadium in Egypt and Africa.

spots.name: Green Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Green Synagogue was a former Jewish synagogue, that was located near Wabour Al Mey, Bab Sharqi, in the Moharam Bek neighborhood, in the Central District of Alexandria, Egypt. The synagogue was completed in 1901 and draws its name from its architect, Abraham Green.

spots.name: White and Blue restaurant

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Greek Club (ENOA: Ellenika Nautikos Olimnos Alexandria) is a private club but with two public restaurants, and something of an Alex institution. Ride the elevator up to Olive Island Restaurant on the third floor: the place is dark and piled high with old furniture. So ride back down to the second floor which has White and Blue Restaurant out on the terrace, overlooking the eastern harbour. A f

spots.name: Athineos

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The "Mermaid of Alexandria" is a local legend frequented by both Durrell and Cavafy, but alas, it has fallen far since its glory days. The views are still amazing, and the Greek motifs in the gilded friezes and stenciled frescoes give some character, but the food is, despite the Greek names on the menu, almost entirely Arabized: order souvlaki and you'll get kebab.

spots.name: Mermaid Bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Little and nice bar with good view to the sea. Prices on beer are moderate; hard liquor is more expensive. At night the upper floor has a dance floor featuring Western and Arabic music. The bar is frequented by foreign (particularly American) Arabic language students at the Teaching Arabic as a Foreign Language (TAFL) Center at Alexandria University.

spots.name: Trianon

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Historic, posh cafe and restaurant in the heart of Alexandria dating back to 1905, this is where the creme de la creme of Alexandrian society like singer Om Kolthoum and Cavafy used to hang around. The glory days are long over, but Trianon remains famous for what is said to be the country's best om ali, a rich Egyptian take on bread pudding.

spots.name: La Veranda

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Very central downtown, near the Metropole, Cecil and Sofitel hotels. Within, most of the floor space is the cafe-patisserie Jardin Delices. About a quarter is La Veranda restaurant, with good European/East Med cuisine. Serves alcohol. Atmospheric with the old posters, but nowadays not a spy or dilapidated duchess to be found.

spots.name: Ibn El-Balad Gleem
spots.summary: Two-storey restaurant, now part of THM chain. First floor has grilled meats featuring their famous Ibn al-Balad fattah. The second floor serves seafood. Both get great scores for food, service and ambiance.

spots.name: Chicken Tikka
spots.summary: Delicious Egyptian food, with views of the harbour and Fort Qait Bey. Try the shish kebab and the wara' el enab (stuffed vine leaves). There is a second restaurant of this chain in 426 El-Gaish Rd., Luran.

spots.name: Foul Mohamed Ahmed

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Legendary joint for fuul and falafel, clean, friendly and inexpensive. According to a personal memory by an Alexandrian lady it was in Jewish ownership and called Binyamin before the Revolution of 1952.

spots.name: Spitfire Bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Cheerful bar with food a short block off the main downtown street. "Atmospheric", meaning the building looks derelict, but persevere.

spots.name: Tawn Coffe Shop

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Yes, "Coffe". Great place on the Corniche, with a decent pizza and chairs in front of the café for "enjoying" the traffic and view.

spots.name: Clay Cafe

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Coffee and stuff are only just okay for the price, you come for the laidback atmosphere and the wi-fi.

spots.name: Abou Shakra

spots.summary: Popular Egyptian chain for shwarms, similar grills and set meals of kebab, kofta, fries and salad.

spots.name: Balbaa
spots.summary: Popular place for Egyptian meat and seafood. Their outlet at Carrefour City Center has closed.

spots.name: Sheikh Ali

spots.summary: Better known among travellers as the Cap d'Or and one of Alexandria's oldest bars.

spots.summary: Possibly the best Italian restaurant in town, serving pizza and pasta since 1979.

spots.name: Club21

spots.summary: Friendly inexpensive place for food and drink, plus shisha in the garden.

spots.name: Ole Cafe
spots.summary: A reasonably priced restaurant with Spanish cuisine. Try the Beef Madrid.

spots.summary: Relaxing place on the waterfront.
